```ts
/**
 * @generated by patterns — regenerate rather than edit.
 * @pattern tool-loop
 * @options eb4816015c5ba2ad
 */

/**
 * The ask-call-answer cycle, run until the model has an answer.
 *
 * One model call per step. Every tool the model asked for is run, the results
 * go back as the next turn, and the loop goes round again — until the model
 * replies with text instead of a call, or a bound is reached. What comes back
 * is the answer plus the whole transcript, which is what you send to continue
 * the conversation and what you read to find out what happened.
 *
 * Nothing here is imported. The model arrives through the one-method interface
 * below, which the chat-model port's `ChatModel` satisfies as it stands, and
 * the messages this appends are that port's own — checked with the compiler,
 * because a transcript a provider rejects is the failure this pattern exists to
 * prevent.
 *
 * Several calls in one turn run one at a time, in the order the model listed
 * them. That is what tools sharing state need, and what a tool behind a rate
 * limit or a single connection needs.
 *
 * A tool that throws ends the run, carrying the call and every step taken so
 * far. That is the reading for a caller where a failed tool means the request
 * is over — no further tokens are spent on a model that cannot succeed.
 */

/**
 * The model and the conversation, as narrowly as this pattern needs them.
 *
 * These are the shapes the mainstream provider abstractions agree on, under the
 * names the chat-model port uses. If you generated that port, its `ChatModel`
 * is a `LoopModel` already and its `Message` is this one — verified in both
 * directions, including the two messages this file appends.
 */

/**
 * A schema as the wire carries it: a JSON Schema object, unexamined.
 */
export type JsonSchema = Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;

/**
 * A run of text from the model.
 */
export interface TextPart {
  readonly type: "text";
  readonly text: string;
}

/**
 * The model asking for a tool to be run.
 *
 * `input` is `unknown` and already a value — an adapter that received it as a
 * JSON string is what parsed it. It is whatever the model produced, though,
 * which is why a tool declares how to read it rather than being handed
 * something trusted.
 */
export interface ToolCallPart {
  readonly type: "tool-call";
  readonly callId: string;
  readonly toolName: string;
  readonly input: unknown;
}

/**
 * What running a tool produced, on its way back to the model.
 *
 * `callId` has to be the one the call carried. Both mainstream formats reject a
 * conversation in which an assistant's tool call has no matching result, and
 * neither pairs them by order.
 */
export interface ToolResultPart {
  readonly type: "tool-result";
  readonly callId: string;
  readonly toolName: string;
  readonly output: unknown;
  readonly failed?: boolean;
}

/**
 * The conversation, as three roles.
 *
 * An assistant turn holds text and calls in one list, which is what lets a
 * response be appended without reshaping — the step below that appends one is a
 * single line because of it.
 */
export interface UserMessage {
  readonly role: "user";
  readonly content: readonly TextPart[];
}

export interface AssistantMessage {
  readonly role: "assistant";
  readonly content: readonly (TextPart | ToolCallPart)[];
}

export interface ToolMessage {
  readonly role: "tool";
  readonly content: readonly ToolResultPart[];
}

export type Message = UserMessage | AssistantMessage | ToolMessage;

/**
 * A tool as the model is shown it. Built below from the box, rather than
 * written twice.
 */
export interface ToolDefinition {
  readonly name: string;
  readonly description?: string;
  readonly inputSchema: JsonSchema;
}

/**
 * Tokens in and out, where the provider reported them.
 *
 * Present and possibly `undefined` rather than optional, so reading one is a
 * check for `undefined` rather than a check for a missing property.
 */
export interface Usage {
  readonly inputTokens: number | undefined;
  readonly outputTokens: number | undefined;
}

/**
 * What this pattern sends. Every field is one the chat-model port's request
 * also has.
 */
export interface ModelRequest {
  readonly messages: readonly Message[];
  readonly system?: string;
  readonly tools?: readonly ToolDefinition[];
  readonly toolChoice?:
    | { readonly mode: "auto" }
    | { readonly mode: "none" }
    | { readonly mode: "required" }
    | { readonly mode: "tool"; readonly toolName: string };
  readonly maxOutputTokens?: number;
  readonly temperature?: number;
  readonly signal?: AbortSignal;
  readonly providerOptions?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
}

/**
 * One turn of output.
 *
 * `finishReason` is a `string` rather than a union, and `warnings` is optional,
 * so that a model written for a test fits without either — while a real
 * response, which has both, fits too.
 */
export interface ModelAnswer {
  readonly content: readonly (TextPart | ToolCallPart)[];
  readonly finishReason: string;
  readonly usage: Usage;
  readonly warnings?: readonly string[];
}

/**
 * The model.
 *
 * A method rather than a function property. Method parameters are checked
 * bivariantly and a property's contravariantly under `strictFunctionTypes`, so
 * a method is the spelling that accepts a `generate` whose request type is
 * compatible without being identical — which is every real one, since none of
 * them were written against this file.
 *
 * One method, and it takes everything. A model with configuration methods is
 * one whose state the loop would have to reason about between steps.
 */
export interface LoopModel {
  generate(request: ModelRequest): Promise<ModelAnswer>;
}

/**
 * The tools, and the factory that is the only way to build one.
 *
 * This is where the pattern's one piece of type-level work is. The loop looks a
 * tool up by a name the *model* produced, so the key is a `string` and there is
 * no type parameter it could carry — which means the box cannot be declared
 * over each tool's input type. Declaring it over `unknown` looks right and is
 * refused, because an executor taking an `Order` is not one taking `unknown`.
 * So the input type is closed over instead: `tool` is generic in it, `execute`
 * receives it, and the loop receives a `run` that takes `unknown` because
 * `unknown` is all the loop has.
 */

/**
 * What the loop was told about the call it is running.
 *
 * `signal` is the one the run was given, so a tool that makes a network call
 * can pass it straight to `fetch` and be cancelled with everything else.
 * Present and possibly `undefined`, so a tool reads it the same way whether or
 * not the caller supplied one.
 */
export interface ToolContext {
  readonly callId: string;
  readonly toolName: string;
  /** Which step asked, counted from one. */
  readonly step: number;
  readonly signal: AbortSignal | undefined;
}

/**
 * A tool, as the caller writes it.
 *
 * `parse` is required, and that is deliberate. The input came from a language
 * model: it is the least trustworthy value in the system, and a truncated tool
 * call arrives here as an object missing half its fields. Writing `parse: (raw)
 * => raw as Order` is available and is a decision that then appears at the call
 * site, rather than one nobody made.
 *
 * It is also what gives `execute` a type. `Input` is inferred from what `parse`
 * returns, so `execute`'s argument needs no annotation and cannot disagree with
 * it.
 *
 * A schema library fits here directly: `parse: (raw) => OrderSchema.parse(raw)`
 * for Zod, or any function that returns the value or throws. A throw is
 * reported the same way a failing tool is.
 */
export interface ToolSpec<Input, Output> {
  /**
   * Read by the model. The one field here that changes how well the tool gets
   * used.
   */
  readonly description?: string;
  readonly inputSchema: JsonSchema;
  readonly parse: (raw: unknown) => Input | Promise<Input>;
  readonly execute: (
    input: Input,
    context: ToolContext,
  ) => Output | Promise<Output>;
}

/**
 * A tool, as the loop holds it.
 *
 * No input type and no name. No input type because there is nothing the loop
 * could do with one — it dispatches on a string. No name because the box is
 * keyed by name, and a tool carrying a second copy is a tool whose name can
 * disagree with the one it answers to.
 */
export interface Tool {
  readonly description?: string;
  readonly inputSchema: JsonSchema;
  readonly run: (raw: unknown, context: ToolContext) => Promise<unknown>;
}

/**
 * The tools available, keyed by the name the model will use.
 *
 * Short, stable names are worth caring about: each one is in the model's
 * context on every step.
 */
export type Toolbox = Readonly<Record<string, Tool>>;

/**
 * Builds a tool, keeping its input type to itself.
 *
 * The returned `Tool` has no `Input` in it, which is the point: a record of
 * tools with different input types is a record of `Tool`, and every executor
 * still gets its own argument type. Nothing here casts, and nothing the caller
 * writes needs to.
 */
export function tool<Input, Output>(spec: ToolSpec<Input, Output>): Tool {
  return {
    inputSchema: spec.inputSchema,
    ...(spec.description === undefined
      ? {}
      : { description: spec.description }),
    run: async (raw: unknown, context: ToolContext): Promise<unknown> =>
      spec.execute(await spec.parse(raw), context),
  };
}

/**
 * The tools as the model is shown them, built from the box.
 *
 * Derived rather than declared beside it, so a tool cannot be in the box and
 * missing from the request, or described one way to the model and another in
 * the code.
 */
function definitionsOf(tools: Toolbox): readonly ToolDefinition[] {
  return Object.entries(tools).map(([name, declared]) => ({
    name,
    inputSchema: declared.inputSchema,
    ...(declared.description === undefined
      ? {}
      : { description: declared.description }),
  }));
}

/**
 * The reason a tool gave, as a string.
 *
 * A tool can throw anything, so this is a `String()` away from whatever it was.
 */
function reasonOf(cause: unknown): string {
  return cause instanceof Error ? cause.message : String(cause);
}

/**
 * One turn of the loop: what the model said, and what running it produced.
 *
 * Kept whole rather than reduced to its text, because the interesting questions
 * after a run are about the calls — which tools ran, in what order, with what —
 * and a step that had thrown them away could not answer any of them.
 */
export interface Step {
  /** Counted from one. */
  readonly index: number;
  /** The assistant turn, exactly as it was appended to the transcript. */
  readonly content: readonly (TextPart | ToolCallPart)[];
  /**
   * What the model said in words. Empty on a turn that only asked for tools.
   */
  readonly text: string;
  readonly toolCalls: readonly ToolCallPart[];
  /**
   * One per call, in the order of the calls. Empty on the turn that answered.
   */
  readonly toolResults: readonly ToolResultPart[];
  readonly finishReason: string;
  readonly usage: Usage;
  /** Whatever the provider said about this turn. Empty when it said nothing. */
  readonly warnings: readonly string[];
}

/**
 * Why the loop stopped.
 *
 * `"answer"` is the one you want: the model replied with text instead of a
 * call, which is the loop's own exit.
 *
 * The other two are bounds. `"max-steps"` means the model was still asking when
 * the count ran out, and `"stop-condition"` means one of the conditions said to
 * stop — checked in that order, so a condition that matched on the last allowed
 * step is reported as the condition it was.
 */
export type StopReason = "answer" | "max-steps" | "stop-condition";

/**
 * What a run produces.
 *
 * `messages` is the whole conversation including what was passed in, so
 * continuing is a matter of appending to it and running again — no reassembly,
 * and no chance of dropping the pairing between a call and its result.
 *
 * `usage` is summed over every step rather than taken from the last, because a
 * loop's cost is the loop's, not the final turn's.
 */
export interface ToolLoopResult {
  /**
   * The final turn's text. Empty when the run ended on a bound rather than an
   * answer.
   */
  readonly text: string;
  readonly steps: readonly Step[];
  readonly messages: readonly Message[];
  readonly usage: Usage;
  readonly stoppedBy: StopReason;
}

/**
 * A tool failed, and `onToolError: "throw"` was chosen at generation time.
 *
 * Everything needed to see what happened travels: which tool, which call, the
 * input it was given, what the tool threw — as `cause`, which is `unknown`
 * because a tool may throw anything — and every step up to this one, so the
 * transcript is not lost along with the run.
 *
 * A name no tool has arrives here too. That is the model's mistake rather than
 * a tool's, and the message says which it was.
 */
export class ToolFailedError extends Error {
  readonly toolName: string;
  readonly callId: string;
  /** What the model sent, which is usually where the answer is. */
  readonly input: unknown;
  /** Every step before this one, in order. */
  readonly steps: readonly Step[];

  constructor(call: ToolCallPart, cause: unknown, steps: readonly Step[]) {
    // `cause` through the standard option rather than a field of the same name:
    // a field would shadow `Error.cause` and needs an `override` to say so, and
    // this is where anything reading an error already looks.
    super(`the tool "${call.toolName}" failed: ${reasonOf(cause)}`, { cause });
    this.name = "ToolFailedError";
    this.toolName = call.toolName;
    this.callId = call.callId;
    this.input = call.input;
    this.steps = steps;
  }
}

/**
 * The stopping conditions.
 *
 * A condition is a function of the steps so far, checked after each one that
 * ran tools — not after the turn that answered, since a run the model has
 * finished is over for a better reason. They are pure and take the whole
 * history, so a condition can be about the shape of the run rather than only
 * about its last step.
 */

/**
 * Whether the run should stop, given everything that has happened.
 */
export type StopCondition = (steps: readonly Step[]) => boolean;

/**
 * Stops after a turn that called a particular tool.
 *
 * This is how a tool becomes the run's answer: give the model a `submitAnswer`
 * and stop when it uses it, and the loop ends on the model's decision rather
 * than on a bound. The result's `text` will be empty, and what you want is in
 * that call's input.
 */
export function hasToolCall(toolName: string): StopCondition {
  return (steps: readonly Step[]): boolean => {
    const last = steps.at(-1);
    return (
      last !== undefined &&
      last.toolCalls.some((call) => call.toolName === toolName)
    );
  };
}

/**
 * Stops when a tool has been called twice with the same input.
 *
 * The loop this catches is the common one: a model that reads a result, does
 * not get what it needed from it, and asks the identical question again.
 * `maxSteps` bounds that too, but only by spending the whole budget first.
 *
 * The comparison is on the serialised input, so two objects with the same
 * fields in a different order are not equal. That is the honest bound rather
 * than a bug — a model repeating itself sends the same thing the same way — and
 * it is why this is a condition you opt into rather than the loop's own rule. A
 * tool that is *meant* to be called twice with the same input, polling for a
 * status, wants `maxSteps` and not this.
 */
export function repeatedCall(): StopCondition {
  return (steps: readonly Step[]): boolean => {
    const seen = new Set<string>();

    for (const step of steps) {
      for (const call of step.toolCalls) {
        // `String` rather than the value: `JSON.stringify(undefined)` is
        // `undefined`, and two calls with no input at all are still the same
        // call.
        const key = `${call.toolName}:${String(JSON.stringify(call.input))}`;

        if (seen.has(key)) {
          return true;
        }
        seen.add(key);
      }
    }

    return false;
  };
}

/**
 * Stops once the run has spent a number of tokens.
 *
 * Checked after a step, so this is where spending stops rather than a ceiling
 * it cannot cross: the step that goes over the line has already been paid for.
 * Sizing it below the real limit is the point.
 *
 * Steps whose provider reported no usage count as nothing, which means a
 * provider that reports none makes this condition never fire. Worth knowing
 * before it is the only thing standing between a stuck loop and a bill.
 */
export function tokenBudget(tokens: number): StopCondition {
  return (steps: readonly Step[]): boolean => {
    const spent = steps.reduce(
      (total, step) =>
        total + (step.usage.inputTokens ?? 0) + (step.usage.outputTokens ?? 0),
      0,
    );

    return spent >= tokens;
  };
}

/**
 * How many model calls a run may make before it stops asking.
 *
 * Eight is enough for a task that needs a few lookups and small enough that a
 * stuck run is cheap. It is a bound rather than an expectation: a run that
 * reaches it has usually gone wrong.
 */
const DEFAULT_MAX_STEPS = 8;

/**
 * One run of the loop.
 *
 * `messages` is the conversation so far, which on a first run is one user
 * message and on a continuation is the previous result's `messages` with a new
 * one appended.
 */
export interface ToolLoopRequest {
  readonly messages: readonly Message[];
  readonly tools: Toolbox;
  readonly system?: string;
  /** Defaults to eight. Has to be a positive integer. */
  readonly maxSteps?: number;
  /**
   * Any number of reasons to stop early, checked after each step that ran
   * tools. The first one that says so ends the run.
   */
  readonly stopWhen?: readonly StopCondition[];
  readonly maxOutputTokens?: number;
  readonly temperature?: number;
  /**
   * Cancels the run. Checked before each model call, passed to the model, and
   * handed to every tool through its context — so one signal stops all three.
   */
  readonly signal?: AbortSignal;
  readonly providerOptions?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
  /**
   * Called with each step as it completes, which is what a progress display
   * wants. Anything it throws comes out of the run.
   */
  readonly onStep?: (step: Step) => void;
}

/**
 * Runs the loop until the model answers or a bound is reached.
 *
 * Throws only for a cancelled run, a `maxSteps` that is not a positive integer,
 * and whatever the model itself throws, plus `ToolFailedError` for a tool that
 * failed.
 *
 * The transcript is built as it goes and returned whichever way the run ends,
 * so nothing that was paid for is lost.
 */
export async function runToolLoop(
  model: LoopModel,
  request: ToolLoopRequest,
): Promise<ToolLoopResult> {
  const maxSteps = request.maxSteps ?? DEFAULT_MAX_STEPS;

  if (!Number.isInteger(maxSteps) || maxSteps < 1) {
    throw new RangeError(
      `maxSteps has to be a positive integer, and was ${String(request.maxSteps)}`,
    );
  }

  // Built once. The model is shown the same tools on every step, and deriving
  // them per step would be the same list at a cost per round trip.
  const definitions = definitionsOf(request.tools);
  const messages: Message[] = [...request.messages];
  const steps: Step[] = [];

  for (let index = 1; index <= maxSteps; index += 1) {
    // Before the call rather than after, so a signal aborted before the run
    // starts costs nothing.
    request.signal?.throwIfAborted();

    const answer = await model.generate(asked(request, messages, definitions));
    const calls = answer.content.filter(
      (part): part is ToolCallPart => part.type === "tool-call",
    );

    // The turn goes back exactly as it arrived. Reshaping it here is what
    // breaks the pairing between a call and the result that answers it.
    messages.push({ role: "assistant", content: answer.content });

    if (calls.length === 0) {
      // The model spoke instead of asking, which is what the loop has been
      // waiting for.
      const answered = stepOf(index, answer, calls, []);
      steps.push(answered);
      request.onStep?.(answered);

      return resultOf(steps, messages, "answer");
    }

    const results = await answerCalls(calls, request, index, steps);
    // One tool message per turn, holding one result per call — not one message
    // per result, which is a shape neither format accepts here.
    messages.push({ role: "tool", content: results });

    const taken = stepOf(index, answer, calls, results);
    steps.push(taken);
    request.onStep?.(taken);

    if ((request.stopWhen ?? []).some((condition) => condition(steps))) {
      return resultOf(steps, messages, "stop-condition");
    }
  }

  // Still asking when the count ran out. The transcript is the useful part of
  // this.
  return resultOf(steps, messages, "max-steps");
}

/**
 * The request for one step.
 *
 * The messages are copied. The loop appends to its own list as it goes, and a
 * request holding that list rather than a copy of it would keep changing after
 * it was sent — so a logged request, a recorded one, or a retry built from one
 * would show a conversation that is not the one the model answered. One copy
 * per step against one network round trip is not a cost worth thinking about.
 *
 * The optional fields are spread in only when they were given, rather than
 * written as `undefined`. A project with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` needs
 * that, and a provider that distinguishes an absent field from a null one needs
 * it too.
 *
 * `tools` and `toolChoice` go together and are both left out when the box is
 * empty: an empty tools array is a request some providers reject, and a run
 * with no tools is one model call rather than a loop.
 */
function asked(
  request: ToolLoopRequest,
  messages: readonly Message[],
  definitions: readonly ToolDefinition[],
): ModelRequest {
  return {
    messages: [...messages],
    ...(definitions.length === 0
      ? {}
      : { tools: definitions, toolChoice: { mode: "auto" } }),
    ...(request.system === undefined ? {} : { system: request.system }),
    ...(request.maxOutputTokens === undefined
      ? {}
      : { maxOutputTokens: request.maxOutputTokens }),
    ...(request.temperature === undefined
      ? {}
      : { temperature: request.temperature }),
    ...(request.signal === undefined ? {} : { signal: request.signal }),
    ...(request.providerOptions === undefined
      ? {}
      : { providerOptions: request.providerOptions }),
  };
}

/**
 * Runs every call in one turn, and returns one result per call.
 *
 * In order, one at a time. A tool does not start until the one before it has
 * finished, which is what tools touching the same state need.
 *
 * The first failure ends the run, and the calls after it never start. That is
 * the other half of what sequential means: an ordered run that continued past a
 * failed step would be running on state that was not established.
 */
async function answerCalls(
  calls: readonly ToolCallPart[],
  request: ToolLoopRequest,
  step: number,
  steps: readonly Step[],
): Promise<readonly ToolResultPart[]> {
  const results: ToolResultPart[] = [];

  for (const call of calls) {
    results.push(await answerOf(call, request, step, steps));
  }

  return results;
}

/**
 * Runs one call.
 *
 * A tool that threw and a name no tool has are the same thing here — a call
 * that cannot be answered — and both end the run.
 */
async function answerOf(
  call: ToolCallPart,
  request: ToolLoopRequest,
  step: number,
  steps: readonly Step[],
): Promise<ToolResultPart> {
  const found = request.tools[call.toolName];

  if (found === undefined) {
    throw new ToolFailedError(
      call,
      new Error(`no tool named "${call.toolName}" is available`),
      steps,
    );
  }

  try {
    const output = await found.run(
      call.input,
      contextOf(call, step, request.signal),
    );

    return {
      type: "tool-result",
      callId: call.callId,
      toolName: call.toolName,
      output,
    };
  } catch (cause) {
    throw new ToolFailedError(call, cause, steps);
  }
}

/**
 * What a tool is told about the call it is running.
 */
function contextOf(
  call: ToolCallPart,
  step: number,
  signal: AbortSignal | undefined,
): ToolContext {
  return { callId: call.callId, toolName: call.toolName, step, signal };
}

/**
 * One step, from the turn that produced it.
 *
 * The calls are passed in rather than filtered again, so the step's list is the
 * same list the loop ran — one place for it to be wrong instead of two.
 */
function stepOf(
  index: number,
  answer: ModelAnswer,
  toolCalls: readonly ToolCallPart[],
  toolResults: readonly ToolResultPart[],
): Step {
  return {
    index,
    content: answer.content,
    text: textOf(answer.content),
    toolCalls,
    toolResults,
    finishReason: answer.finishReason,
    usage: answer.usage,
    warnings: answer.warnings ?? [],
  };
}

/**
 * Everything the model said in a turn, as one string.
 *
 * Joined with nothing between the runs, because they are pieces of one sentence
 * and a separator lands in the middle of it.
 */
function textOf(content: readonly (TextPart | ToolCallPart)[]): string {
  return content
    .filter((part): part is TextPart => part.type === "text")
    .map((part) => part.text)
    .join("");
}

/**
 * The result, however the run ended.
 */
function resultOf(
  steps: readonly Step[],
  messages: readonly Message[],
  stoppedBy: StopReason,
): ToolLoopResult {
  return {
    text: steps.at(-1)?.text ?? "",
    steps,
    messages,
    usage: totalOf(steps),
    stoppedBy,
  };
}

/**
 * What the whole run cost.
 *
 * A field stays `undefined` when no step reported it, rather than becoming
 * zero: a provider that reports nothing and a run that used nothing are
 * different answers, and only one of them is worth acting on.
 */
function totalOf(steps: readonly Step[]): Usage {
  return {
    inputTokens: added(steps.map((step) => step.usage.inputTokens)),
    outputTokens: added(steps.map((step) => step.usage.outputTokens)),
  };
}

function added(counts: readonly (number | undefined)[]): number | undefined {
  const reported = counts.filter(
    (count): count is number => count !== undefined,
  );

  return reported.length === 0
    ? undefined
    : reported.reduce((total, count) => total + count, 0);
}
```

## tool-loop-example.ts (example)

```ts
/**
 * @generated by patterns — regenerate rather than edit.
 * @pattern tool-loop
 * @options eb4816015c5ba2ad
 */

/**
 * A model given two tools and left to use them.
 *
 * The tools here read from an object and write to it. In real code they call a
 * database and a payments API, and nothing else below changes — which is the
 * point of the box being a plain record.
 */

import {
  ToolFailedError,
  repeatedCall,
  runToolLoop,
  tokenBudget,
  tool,
} from "./tool-loop.js";
import type {
  LoopModel,
  ToolLoopRequest,
  ToolLoopResult,
  Toolbox,
} from "./tool-loop.js";

/**
 * The world these tools act on. A database, in a real one.
 */
interface Order {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly total: number;
  refunded: boolean;
}

const ORDERS = new Map<string, Order>([
  ["A-1", { id: "A-1", total: 41.5, refunded: false }],
]);

/**
 * What both tools take, and where the model's input stops being untrusted.
 *
 * A plain function, which is all `parse` ever is. With a schema library this is
 * `OrderRef.parse(raw)` and the tools below do not change — and the message it
 * throws is read by the model, so it says what to do rather than what happened.
 */
interface OrderRef {
  readonly orderId: string;
}

function orderRef(raw: unknown): OrderRef {
  const record =
    typeof raw === "object" && raw !== null
      ? (raw as Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>)
      : {};
  const orderId = record["orderId"];

  if (typeof orderId !== "string") {
    throw new Error("orderId has to be a string");
  }

  return { orderId };
}

/**
 * The tools.
 *
 * Note what is *not* written: neither `execute` annotates its argument. The
 * type comes from `parse`, so the two cannot disagree and there is one place
 * the input's shape is stated.
 *
 * The descriptions are the field worth spending time on. They are the only
 * thing telling the model when to reach for one of these.
 */
export const TOOLS: Toolbox = {
  lookupOrder: tool({
    description:
      "Look up an order by its id. Returns the total and whether it was refunded.",
    inputSchema: {
      type: "object",
      properties: { orderId: { type: "string" } },
      required: ["orderId"],
    },
    parse: orderRef,
    // `input.orderId` is a string here, inferred from `orderRef`.
    execute: (input) => {
      const found = ORDERS.get(input.orderId);

      if (found === undefined) {
        throw new Error(`no order ${input.orderId}`);
      }

      return { total: found.total, refunded: found.refunded };
    },
  }),

  refundOrder: tool({
    description: "Refund an order in full. Only ever call this once per order.",
    inputSchema: {
      type: "object",
      properties: { orderId: { type: "string" } },
      required: ["orderId"],
    },
    parse: orderRef,
    execute: (input, context) => {
      const found = ORDERS.get(input.orderId);

      if (found === undefined) {
        throw new Error(`no order ${input.orderId}`);
      }

      if (found.refunded) {
        // The model asking twice is a failure it can read and recover from.
        throw new Error(`order ${input.orderId} was already refunded`);
      }

      // The run's own signal, so a cancelled run cancels the call this would
      // make.
      context.signal?.throwIfAborted();
      found.refunded = true;

      return { refunded: found.total };
    },
  }),
};

/**
 * Answers a customer, using the tools as it needs them.
 *
 * Two conditions beyond the step count. `repeatedCall` ends a run where the
 * model has stopped making progress, and `tokenBudget` ends one that is making
 * progress too expensively.
 *
 * A tool that fails ends the run, so the failure is caught rather than read out
 * of the transcript.
 */
export async function handle(
  model: LoopModel,
  question: string,
): Promise<ToolLoopResult | undefined> {
  try {
    const run = await runToolLoop(model, requestFor(question));

    summarise(run);

    return run;
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof ToolFailedError) {
      // The steps are on the error, so the run is still readable.
      report(
        `${error.toolName} failed after ${String(error.steps.length)} steps`,
      );
      report(`it was given ${JSON.stringify(error.input)}`);

      return undefined;
    }
    // A cancelled run, a transport failure: not this function's to interpret.
    throw error;
  }
}

/**
 * Everything about the run except the question.
 */
function requestFor(question: string): ToolLoopRequest {
  return {
    tools: TOOLS,
    system:
      "You help customers with orders. Look an order up before refunding it.",
    messages: [{ role: "user", content: [{ type: "text", text: question }] }],
    maxSteps: 6,
    stopWhen: [repeatedCall(), tokenBudget(20_000)],
    temperature: 0,
    onStep: (step) => {
      // A progress line per turn, which is what a caller watching this wants.
      report(
        `step ${String(step.index)}: ${String(step.toolCalls.length)} calls`,
      );
    },
  };
}

/**
 * What the run did, read off the result.
 *
 * `stoppedBy` is the field to check first: a run that ended on a bound has a
 * transcript worth keeping and usually no answer in it.
 */
function summarise(run: ToolLoopResult): void {
  if (run.stoppedBy === "answer") {
    report(run.text);
  } else {
    report(`stopped early: ${run.stoppedBy}`);
  }

  for (const step of run.steps) {
    for (const result of step.toolResults) {
      const mark = result.failed === true ? "failed" : "ok";
      report(
        `  ${result.toolName} (${mark}): ${JSON.stringify(result.output)}`,
      );
    }
  }

  report(
    `${String(run.usage.outputTokens ?? 0)} tokens out over ${String(run.steps.length)} steps`,
  );
}

/**
 * Where this example's output goes. A logger, a span, a test spy.
 */
function report(line: string): void {
  void line;
}
```

```ts
/**
 * @generated by patterns — regenerate rather than edit.
 * @pattern tool-loop
 * @options eb4816015c5ba2ad
 */

/**
 * The loop, against scripted models and tools that record what they were given.
 *
 * A model is a function returning a recorded turn, so every case here is a
 * shape a real provider produces and none of them go near a network. What is
 * being pinned is the transcript, the pairing of a result with its call, the
 * order the tools ran in, and each of the ways a run can end.
 */

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import {
  ToolFailedError,
  hasToolCall,
  repeatedCall,
  runToolLoop,
  tokenBudget,
  tool,
} from "./tool-loop.js";
import type {
  LoopModel,
  Message,
  ModelAnswer,
  ModelRequest,
  Step,
  ToolLoopRequest,
  ToolLoopResult,
  Toolbox,
  Usage,
} from "./tool-loop.js";

/**
 * A model that answers from a script, and tools that record what they ran.
 *
 * The last answer repeats, so a case that expects three steps does not have to
 * say what a fourth would have received.
 */

const USAGE: Usage = { inputTokens: 10, outputTokens: 4 };

function says(text: string): ModelAnswer {
  return {
    content: [{ type: "text", text }],
    finishReason: "stop",
    usage: USAGE,
  };
}

function asks(
  ...calls: readonly (readonly [
    name: string,
    input: unknown,
    callId?: string,
  ])[]
): ModelAnswer {
  return {
    content: calls.map(([toolName, input, callId], at) => ({
      type: "tool-call" as const,
      callId: callId ?? `call-${String(at + 1)}`,
      toolName,
      input,
    })),
    finishReason: "tool-calls",
    usage: USAGE,
  };
}

/** A model answering from a list, keeping every request it was given. */
function scripted(...answers: readonly ModelAnswer[]): {
  readonly model: LoopModel;
  readonly seen: readonly ModelRequest[];
} {
  const seen: ModelRequest[] = [];
  let at = 0;

  return {
    seen,
    model: {
      generate: (request: ModelRequest) => {
        seen.push(request);
        const answer = answers[Math.min(at, answers.length - 1)];
        at += 1;

        if (answer === undefined) {
          throw new Error("the script was empty");
        }

        return Promise.resolve(answer);
      },
    },
  };
}

/**
 * A toolbox whose tools record their calls in one shared list.
 *
 * `ran` holds a line per call in the order the calls *finished*, which is what
 * makes the difference between running them together and running them in order
 * observable.
 */
function recording(): {
  readonly tools: Toolbox;
  readonly ran: readonly string[];
} {
  const ran: string[] = [];

  return {
    ran,
    tools: {
      slow: tool({
        inputSchema: { type: "object" },
        parse: (raw: unknown): string => String(readField(raw, "of")),
        execute: async (input: string) => {
          await pause(20);
          ran.push(`slow:${input}`);

          return { of: input };
        },
      }),
      quick: tool({
        inputSchema: { type: "object" },
        parse: (raw: unknown): string => String(readField(raw, "of")),
        execute: (input: string) => {
          ran.push(`quick:${input}`);

          return { of: input };
        },
      }),
      broken: tool({
        inputSchema: { type: "object" },
        parse: (raw: unknown): string => String(readField(raw, "of")),
        execute: (input: string) => {
          ran.push(`broken:${input}`);

          throw new Error(`nothing works for ${input}`);
        },
      }),
      strict: tool({
        inputSchema: { type: "object" },
        // Refuses the model's input rather than the tool's own work, which is
        // the other half of what a failed call can mean.
        parse: (raw: unknown): number => {
          const of = readField(raw, "of");

          if (typeof of !== "number") {
            throw new Error("of has to be a number");
          }

          return of;
        },
        execute: (input: number) => {
          ran.push(`strict:${String(input)}`);

          return { doubled: input * 2 };
        },
      }),
    },
  };
}

function readField(raw: unknown, name: string): unknown {
  return typeof raw === "object" && raw !== null
    ? (raw as Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>)[name]
    : undefined;
}

function pause(milliseconds: number): Promise<void> {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    setTimeout(resolve, milliseconds);
  });
}

/**
 * Every tool result in a run, flattened, which is what most cases here are
 * about.
 */
function resultsOf(run: ToolLoopResult): readonly {
  readonly callId: string;
  readonly toolName: string;
  readonly output: unknown;
  readonly failed?: boolean;
}[] {
  return run.steps.flatMap((step: Step) => step.toolResults);
}

/**
 * The roles of a transcript, in order, which is the shape a provider accepts or
 * does not.
 */
function rolesOf(messages: readonly Message[]): readonly string[] {
  return messages.map((message) => message.role);
}

/**
 * The error a call raised, or a failure saying it raised none.
 *
 * Returned rather than asserted so a case can check the type *and* what it
 * carries.
 */
async function refusalFrom(run: () => Promise<unknown>): Promise<unknown> {
  try {
    await run();
  } catch (error) {
    return error;
  }
  throw new Error("expected a refusal, and nothing was thrown");
}

/**
 * Everything but the two fields every case here supplies, so a case names only
 * what it varies.
 */
type Extras = Omit<ToolLoopRequest, "messages" | "tools">;

function ask(
  model: LoopModel,
  tools: Toolbox,
  extras: Extras = {},
): Promise<ToolLoopResult> {
  return runToolLoop(model, {
    tools,
    messages: [{ role: "user", content: [{ type: "text", text: "go" }] }],
    ...extras,
  });
}

describe("the transcript", () => {
  it("a model that answers straight away takes one step and asks for nothing", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(says("nothing to do"));
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools);
    expect(run.text).toBe("nothing to do");
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("answer");
    expect(run.steps).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(run.steps[0]?.toolCalls).toEqual([]);
    // The user turn and the answer, and no tool message between them.
    expect(rolesOf(run.messages)).toEqual(["user", "assistant"]);
  });

  it("a call and its answer are appended as two messages, in that order", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]), says("done"));
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools);
    // Assistant, then tool, then the answering assistant. A provider handed
    // these in any other order rejects the request.
    expect(rolesOf(run.messages)).toEqual([
      "user",
      "assistant",
      "tool",
      "assistant",
    ]);
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("answer");
    expect(run.text).toBe("done");
  });

  it("the assistant turn goes back exactly as the model sent it", async () => {
    const answer = asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]);
    const { model } = scripted(answer, says("done"));
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools);
    const appended = run.messages[1];
    // Not reshaped, not filtered: the same content. A loop that rebuilds this
    // is a loop that drops the parts it did not think about.
    expect(appended?.role).toBe("assistant");
    expect(appended?.content).toEqual(answer.content);
  });

  it("a result carries the id of the call it answers, not its position", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(
      // Ids a provider might really send, in an order that would make pairing
      // by position wrong.
      asks(["quick", { of: "a" }, "zzz"], ["quick", { of: "b" }, "aaa"]),
      says("done"),
    );
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools);
    expect(resultsOf(run).map((result) => result.callId)).toEqual([
      "zzz",
      "aaa",
    ]);
    expect(resultsOf(run).map((result) => result.output)).toEqual([
      { of: "a" },
      { of: "b" },
    ]);
  });

  it("two calls in one turn come back as one tool message holding both", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(
      asks(["quick", { of: "a" }], ["quick", { of: "b" }]),
      says("done"),
    );
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools);
    const toolTurn = run.messages[2];
    expect(rolesOf(run.messages)).toEqual([
      "user",
      "assistant",
      "tool",
      "assistant",
    ]);
    // One message with two results, rather than two messages with one each.
    expect(toolTurn?.role).toBe("tool");
    expect(toolTurn?.content).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  it("the transcript can be handed straight back to continue the conversation", async () => {
    const first = scripted(asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]), says("done"));
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(first.model, tools);
    const second = scripted(says("still done"));
    const again = await runToolLoop(second.model, {
      tools,
      messages: [
        ...run.messages,
        { role: "user", content: [{ type: "text", text: "and?" }] },
      ],
    });
    expect(again.text).toBe("still done");
    // Every turn of the first run, plus the new question. Nothing had to be
    // reassembled.
    expect(rolesOf(second.seen[0]?.messages ?? [])).toEqual([
      "user",
      "assistant",
      "tool",
      "assistant",
      "user",
    ]);
  });

  it("a request the model was given does not change after it was sent", async () => {
    const { model, seen } = scripted(
      asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]),
      says("done"),
    );
    const { tools } = recording();
    await ask(model, tools);
    // The loop appends to its own list as it goes. A request holding that list
    // rather than a copy would show a conversation the model never saw — which
    // is the one thing a recorded request has to get right.
    expect(rolesOf(seen[0]?.messages ?? [])).toEqual(["user"]);
    expect(rolesOf(seen[1]?.messages ?? [])).toEqual([
      "user",
      "assistant",
      "tool",
    ]);
  });

  it("the model is shown every tool in the box, described", async () => {
    const { model, seen } = scripted(says("done"));
    const tools: Toolbox = {
      named: tool({
        description: "what it is for",
        inputSchema: { type: "object" },
        parse: (raw: unknown) => raw,
        execute: () => "ok",
      }),
      bare: tool({
        inputSchema: { type: "string" },
        parse: (raw: unknown) => raw,
        execute: () => "ok",
      }),
    };
    await ask(model, tools);
    expect(seen[0]?.tools).toEqual([
      {
        name: "named",
        description: "what it is for",
        inputSchema: { type: "object" },
      },
      // No `description` key at all rather than one holding `undefined`, which
      // is what a project with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` needs and what some
      // providers reject.
      { name: "bare", inputSchema: { type: "string" } },
    ]);
    expect(seen[0]?.toolChoice).toEqual({ mode: "auto" });
  });

  it("an empty box sends no tools field at all", async () => {
    const { model, seen } = scripted(says("done"));
    const run = await ask(model, {});
    // An empty array is a request some providers refuse, and there is nothing
    // to choose from.
    expect(seen[0]?.tools).toBeUndefined();
    expect(seen[0]?.toolChoice).toBeUndefined();
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("answer");
  });

  it("usage is summed over the run rather than taken from the last turn", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(
      asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]),
      asks(["quick", { of: "b" }]),
      says("done"),
    );
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools);
    expect(run.steps).toHaveLength(3);
    expect(run.usage).toEqual({ inputTokens: 30, outputTokens: 12 });
  });

  it("a run whose provider reported nothing reports nothing rather than zero", async () => {
    const nothing: Usage = { inputTokens: undefined, outputTokens: undefined };
    const { model } = scripted({
      content: [{ type: "text", text: "done" }],
      finishReason: "stop",
      usage: nothing,

    const run = await ask(model, {});

      outputTokens: undefined,

  it("each step is handed over as it completes", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]), says("done"));
    const { tools } = recording();
    const seen: string[] = [];
    await ask(model, tools, {

        seen.push(`${String(step.index)}:${String(step.toolCalls.length)}`);

    expect(seen).toEqual(["1:1", "2:0"]);
  });

  it("a step keeps the text and the calls of its own turn", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(
      {
        content: [
          { type: "text", text: "let me look" },
          {
            type: "tool-call",
            callId: "call-1",
            toolName: "quick",
            input: { of: "a" },

        ],

    const run = await ask(model, tools);
    // A turn can say something *and* ask for a tool, which is a shape worth not
    // losing.
    expect(run.steps[0]?.text).toBe("let me look");
    expect(run.steps[0]?.toolCalls).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(run.steps[0]?.finishReason).toBe("tool-calls");
    // The result's text is the last turn's, not every turn's joined.
    expect(run.text).toBe("done");

  it("the runs of text in one turn are joined with nothing between them", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted({
      content: [
        { type: "text", text: "half" },
        { type: "text", text: "way" },
      ],
      finishReason: "stop",
      usage: USAGE,
    });
    const run = await ask(model, {});
    // Streamed text arrives in pieces of one sentence, so anything between them
    // lands mid-word.
    expect(run.text).toBe("halfway");
  });

  it("what the provider said about a turn is kept with the step", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted({
      content: [{ type: "text", text: "done" }],
      finishReason: "stop",
      usage: USAGE,
      warnings: ["temperature is not supported by this model"],
    });
    const run = await ask(model, {});
    expect(run.steps[0]?.warnings).toEqual([
      "temperature is not supported by this model",
    ]);
  });
});

describe("running the calls in order", () => {
  it("a call does not start until the one before it has finished", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(
      asks(["slow", { of: "a" }], ["quick", { of: "b" }]),
      says("done"),
    );
    const { tools, ran } = recording();
    await ask(model, tools);
    // The order the model listed them in, which is what a tool touching shared
    // state needs. The slow one finished first because it started first.
    expect(ran).toEqual(["slow:a", "quick:b"]);
  });

  it("the results go back in the order of the calls either way", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(
      asks(["slow", { of: "a" }], ["quick", { of: "b" }]),
      says("done"),
    );
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools);
    // The model is reading its own list back, so this order is the calls' and
    // not the clock's.
    expect(resultsOf(run).map((result) => result.toolName)).toEqual([
      "slow",
      "quick",
    ]);
    expect(resultsOf(run).map((result) => result.output)).toEqual([
      { of: "a" },
      { of: "b" },
    ]);
  });
});

describe("a tool that failed", () => {
  it("ends the run, carrying the call and the steps taken so far", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(
      asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]),
      asks(["broken", { of: "b" }]),
      says("unreached"),
    );
    const { tools } = recording();
    const refusal = await refusalFrom(() => ask(model, tools));
    expect(refusal).toBeInstanceOf(ToolFailedError);
    const failed = refusal as ToolFailedError;
    expect(failed.toolName).toBe("broken");
    expect(failed.callId).toBe("call-1");
    expect(failed.input).toEqual({ of: "b" });
    expect(failed.message).toContain("nothing works for b");
    // The first step survived the failure, which is the point of carrying it.
    expect(failed.steps).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(failed.steps[0]?.toolResults[0]?.output).toEqual({ of: "a" });
  });

  it("keeps what the tool threw, whatever it was", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(asks(["odd", {}]), says("unreached"));
    const tools: Toolbox = {
      odd: tool({
        inputSchema: { type: "object" },
        parse: (raw: unknown) => raw,
        execute: () => {
          // A tool may throw anything, which is why `cause` is `unknown`.
          throw "a string, not an error";
        },
      }),
    };
    const refusal = await refusalFrom(() => ask(model, tools));
    expect((refusal as ToolFailedError).cause).toBe("a string, not an error");
    expect((refusal as Error).message).toContain("a string, not an error");
  });

  it("includes a name no tool has, and says which kind of mistake that was", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(
      asks(["imagined", { of: "a" }]),
      says("unreached"),
    );
    const { tools } = recording();
    const refusal = await refusalFrom(() => ask(model, tools));
    expect(refusal).toBeInstanceOf(ToolFailedError);
    expect((refusal as Error).message).toContain("no tool named");
    expect((refusal as ToolFailedError).toolName).toBe("imagined");
  });

    const { model } = scripted(
      asks(["strict", { of: "seven" }]),
      says("unreached"),
    );
    const { tools, ran } = recording();
    const refusal = await refusalFrom(() => ask(model, tools));
    // The parse refused before the body ran, so nothing happened.
    expect(ran).toEqual([]);
    expect((refusal as Error).message).toContain("of has to be a number");
    expect((refusal as ToolFailedError).input).toEqual({ of: "seven" });
  });

  it("does not end a run that has no failing tool in it", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]), says("done"));
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools);
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("answer");
    expect(resultsOf(run)[0]?.output).toEqual({ of: "a" });
  });
});

describe("the ways a run ends", () => {
  it("a model that never stops asking runs out of steps and says so", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]));
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools, { maxSteps: 3 });
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("max-steps");
    expect(run.steps).toHaveLength(3);
    // No answer, and the transcript is what is worth having instead.
    expect(run.text).toBe("");
    expect(rolesOf(run.messages)).toEqual([
      "user",
      "assistant",
      "tool",
      "assistant",
      "tool",
      "assistant",
      "tool",
    ]);
  });

  it("reaching the bound is a result rather than a throw", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]));
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools, { maxSteps: 1 });
    // Everything paid for is still readable, which is the reason for returning.
    expect(run.usage).toEqual({ inputTokens: 10, outputTokens: 4 });
    expect(resultsOf(run)).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it("a step count that is not a positive integer is refused before anything is sent", async () => {
    const { model, seen } = scripted(says("done"));
    for (const maxSteps of [0, -1, 1.5]) {
      const refusal = await refusalFrom(() => ask(model, {}, { maxSteps }));
      expect(refusal).toBeInstanceOf(RangeError);
    }
    expect(seen).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("a signal aborted before the run starts costs nothing", async () => {
    const { model, seen } = scripted(says("done"));
    const refusal = await refusalFrom(() =>
      ask(model, {}, { signal: AbortSignal.abort(new Error("gone")) }),
    );
    expect((refusal as Error).message).toBe("gone");
    // Checked before the call, so no tokens were spent finding out.
    expect(seen).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("the signal reaches the model and every tool", async () => {
    const controller = new AbortController();
    const { model, seen } = scripted(asks(["watching", {}]), says("done"));
    const held: (AbortSignal | undefined)[] = [];
    const tools: Toolbox = {
      watching: tool({
        inputSchema: { type: "object" },
        parse: (raw: unknown) => raw,
        execute: (_input: unknown, context) => {
          held.push(context.signal);
          return "ok";
        },
      }),
    };
    await ask(model, tools, { signal: controller.signal });
    // One signal, so a cancelled run cancels the request and the work it
    // started.
    expect(seen[0]?.signal).toBe(controller.signal);
    expect(held).toEqual([controller.signal]);
  });

  it("a tool is told which call it is answering and which step asked", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(
      asks(["watching", {}], ["watching", {}]),
      says("done"),
    );
    const held: string[] = [];
    const tools: Toolbox = {
      watching: tool({
        inputSchema: { type: "object" },
        parse: (raw: unknown) => raw,
        execute: (_input: unknown, context) =>
          held.push(
            `${context.toolName}/${context.callId}/${String(context.step)}`,
          ),
      }),
    };
    await ask(model, tools);
    expect(held.slice().sort()).toEqual([
      "watching/call-1/1",
      "watching/call-2/1",
    ]);
  });
});

describe("stopping early", () => {
  it("a run stops after the turn that called a chosen tool", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]), says("unreached"));
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools, { stopWhen: [hasToolCall("quick")] });
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("stop-condition");
    expect(run.steps).toHaveLength(1);
    // The tool ran and its result is here: the condition stopped the next ask,
    // not this one.
    expect(resultsOf(run)[0]?.output).toEqual({ of: "a" });
  });

  it("the tool is looked for in the turn that just ran, not in the first one", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(
      asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]),
      asks(["slow", { of: "b" }]),
      says("unreached"),
    );
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools, { stopWhen: [hasToolCall("slow")] });
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("stop-condition");
    // Two turns: the first called something else, and the second is the one
    // that matched.
    expect(run.steps).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  it("a tool that was not called does not stop the run", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]), says("done"));
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools, { stopWhen: [hasToolCall("slow")] });
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("answer");
    expect(run.text).toBe("done");
  });

  it("a model asking the same thing twice is stopped", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]));
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools, {
      maxSteps: 6,
      stopWhen: [repeatedCall()],
    });
    // The second identical call is what trips it, so two steps ran rather than
    // six.
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("stop-condition");
    expect(run.steps).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  it("asking the same tool different things is not repeating itself", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(
      asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]),
      asks(["quick", { of: "b" }]),
      says("done"),
    );
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools, { stopWhen: [repeatedCall()] });
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("answer");
    expect(run.steps).toHaveLength(3);
  });

  it("asking two different tools the same thing is not repeating itself", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(
      asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]),
      asks(["slow", { of: "a" }]),
      says("done"),
    );
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools, { stopWhen: [repeatedCall()] });
    // A repeat is a tool *and* an input, so the same argument to a different
    // tool is a different question.
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("answer");
    expect(run.steps).toHaveLength(3);
  });

  it("two identical calls in one turn are a repeat as much as two turns apart", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(
      asks(["quick", { of: "a" }], ["quick", { of: "a" }]),
      says("unreached"),
    );
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools, { stopWhen: [repeatedCall()] });
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("stop-condition");
    expect(run.steps).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it("a run stops once it has spent its budget", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]));
    const { tools } = recording();
    // Fourteen tokens a step, so the third step is the one that crosses 20.
    const run = await ask(model, tools, {
      maxSteps: 9,
      stopWhen: [tokenBudget(20)],
    });
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("stop-condition");
    expect(run.steps).toHaveLength(2);
    // Over the line, because the step that crossed it had already been paid
    // for.
    expect(run.usage).toEqual({ inputTokens: 20, outputTokens: 8 });
  });

  it("a budget nothing reaches leaves the run to end on its own", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]), says("done"));
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools, { stopWhen: [tokenBudget(10_000)] });
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("answer");
  });

  it("the turn that answers is not put to the conditions", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]), says("done"));
    const { tools } = recording();
    // A condition that always says stop. The answering turn still reports
    // itself as the answer, because a run the model has finished ended for a
    // better reason than a bound.
    const run = await ask(model, tools, { stopWhen: [() => true] });
    expect(run.steps).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("stop-condition");
    const straight = await ask(scripted(says("done")).model, tools, {
      stopWhen: [() => true],
    });
    expect(straight.stoppedBy).toBe("answer");
    expect(straight.text).toBe("done");
  });

  it("the first condition that says so is the one that stops the run", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]));
    const { tools } = recording();
    const asked: number[] = [];
    const run = await ask(model, tools, {
      maxSteps: 4,
      stopWhen: [
        (steps: readonly Step[]) => {
          asked.push(steps.length);
          return false;
        },
        hasToolCall("quick"),
      ],
    });
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("stop-condition");
    // Both were consulted, in order, on the one step that ran.
    expect(asked).toEqual([1]);
  });

  it("a bound reached on the same step as a condition is reported as the condition", async () => {
    const { model } = scripted(asks(["quick", { of: "a" }]));
    const { tools } = recording();
    const run = await ask(model, tools, {
      maxSteps: 1,
      stopWhen: [hasToolCall("quick")],
    });
    // Both were true. The condition is the more specific answer.
    expect(run.stoppedBy).toBe("stop-condition");
  });
});
```
